name: Tri-sets

lead: A tri-set strings together three different exercises without resting between them, then rests before repeating the round. Lifters use it to build muscle in a time-efficient way, which supports the appearance goal of a fuller, more muscular physique.

It is a cousin of the superset, which pairs two exercises. A review of resistance training literature notes that, with volume held constant, supersets and tri-sets shorten workouts but increase perceived exertion.

paras: The three exercises are often for the same muscle group (for example three chest movements) or for different ones. Training logs on bodybuilding forums list tri-sets for back, chest and delts, often at the end of a session, for several rounds with little or no rest within the round.

Fatigue accumulates across the three movements, so weights often drop in later exercises. Same-muscle pairings can lower the total training volume, according to a resistance training review, and fatigue makes careful form important.

chain: High training volume in a short session
More muscle growth stimulus and a fuller physique
angle.text: Tri-sets are a time-saving training method used for hypertrophy. They concentrate volume so the lifter can train a muscle group hard in a shorter session.

lead: A tri-set is a way of organizing a workout in which three different exercises are performed consecutively with no rest between them. After the round the lifter rests and repeats. It is a version of the superset (two exercises back to back) extended to three.[1]

Lifters use tri-sets to condense training: more work in the same time, with a strong local pump in the targeted muscle. Appearance-wise, the aim is hypertrophy, building a bigger, fuller physique. Reference summaries note that training volume has a positive relationship with muscle growth.[1]

On forums such as T Nation, tri-sets appear throughout training logs, for example a back session ending with a pullover, chin-up and shrug tri-set for four rounds with no rest, and a chest session using a three-exercise cable fly tri-set.[2][3]
infobox: Three exercises back to back, then rest

paras: Supersets are pairs of different exercises performed back to back without rest; tri-sets add a third. The strength-training literature notes that same-muscle-group pairs lower training volume, while pairing opposing muscle groups raises it.[1] Rest-period guidance in the same source suggests trained individuals benefit from roughly 3-5 minutes between sets, which is the main trade-off when rests are cut.[1]

Forum logs show a range of uses. One lifter lists a back tri-set of a pullover, chin-ups and plate shrugs for four rounds with no rest.[2] Another posts a chest and shoulder tri-set of machine press, banded drills and lateral raises, taken to failure.[3] A third describes a cable fly tri-set across high, middle and low angles for three rounds.[4] A lifter in another thread called a back-day tri-set at the end of the session fun and extremely challenging, noting he had to drop the weight to complete the reps.[5]

No studies found specific to tri-sets as defined here. A general review of resistance training reports that, holding volume constant, upper-lower supersets and tri-sets shorten workouts but raise perceived exertion.[1]
